channel.title: Wildcard Watch: Linux
channel.description: Exploited vulnerabilities and attacks involving Linux, each with its fix status and first step.

item.title: Patch now: Linux Kernel: Missing Initialization of a Variable
item.description:
Linux Kernel: exploited · fix: 5.10.257, 5.15.208, 6.1.174

First step: Install your Linux distribution's kernel update. The upstream fix is in 5.10.257, 5.15.208 or 6.1.174.

Linux Kernel contains a missing initialization of a variable vulnerability that could allow for unintended modification of page-cache-backed data via failure to preserve the shared-fragment marker during socket buffer coalescing, causing ESP input processing to decrypt shared fragments in place. This vulnerability can be chained with CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 to implant PHP webshells and run commands as root.

High · Fix available · CVE-2026-46300, CVE-2026-98432

item.title: Keep patched: Linux Kernel: 3 flaws exploited together
item.description:
Linux Kernel: Memory corruption (possible RCE) · pre-auth · remote · exploited · fix: 6.1.149, 6.6.103, 6.12.44

First step: Install your Linux distribution's kernel update. The upstream fix is in 6.1.149, 6.6.103 or 6.12.44.

Linux Kernel contains an improper check for unusual or exceptional conditions vulnerability in the TLS receive path which allows a zero-length record retrieved from the rx_list to bypass the intended recvmsg() record-type handling, potentially causing subsequent TLS records to be processed using incorrect zero-copy and queuing assumptions. The impacted product(s) could be end-of-life (EoL) and/or end-of-service (EoS). Users are advised to discontinue use and/or transition to a supported version. CISA lists 2 more flaws in Linux Kernel as exploited on the same day (CVE-2025-39964, CVE-2026-53266).

Critical · Fix available · CVE-2025-39682, CVE-2025-39964, CVE-2026-53266
